note: P4385 (Pro 31:7) — let them drink and forget their poverty, remember their misery no more.

dims.v: compassionate relief — wine given the wretched to forget poverty and misery

the forgetting of poverty and misery that wine may bring the wretched — the compassionate relief offered the perishing and heavy-hearted, a mercy that lets the suffering lay down their grief for a while
the merciful oblivion granted the crushed and suffering

shakach (forget) — 'let them drink and FORGET their poverty and remember their misery no more' (31:7); the same wine that endangers the ruler (31:4-5) is a mercy to the perishing, easing a grief too heavy to bear. Compassion, not indulgence, is the note here (cf 31:6).
